Later this week, a small snag at the desk touched radio checks
Incident Report: Companion Animal Travel Desk Radio Check Disruption

I was on duty at the Companion Animal Travel Desk when the issue began during a routine handoff between desk staff and the cabin team. A traveler came forward with a pet booking that needed confirmation, and the conversation was briefly interrupted by repeated radio static from the boarding area. The static made it difficult to hear the cabin team clearly, and the traveler became concerned that the pet could be delayed. I stayed calm, reassured the traveler, and asked for the details to be repeated in clear terms. The pet travel documents were then reviewed again, and the booking record was checked against the manifest to confirm that the pet was still properly assigned for travel.<<FACT F110>>

After that, I contacted the safety coordinator and asked for a direct radio test with the cabin team. The line improved after the check, and we were able to confirm the needed information without further confusion. I also reminded the desk staff to use short and plain phrases when the signal weakens, which helped reduce the chance of another misunderstanding. The traveler was updated in a warm and respectful manner, and the concern eased once the process was explained.

Following the event, I noted the radio interference in the shift log and asked for the equipment to be reviewed before the next departure wave. I also advised the team to keep a spare contact method ready for animal travel cases, since clear communication is especially important when pets are moving through the airport. No harm came to the animal or the traveler, and the matter was handled smoothly once the call quality improved. The desk remained attentive throughout the shift, and the follow-up steps were completed in good order.
